subject: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope

Team —

I've attached Redline's initial proposal and their pricing model (two tabs: hourly and retainer scenarios). We're evaluating whether to proceed on an hourly ad-hoc engagement for the two upcoming assessments (web app + red team) or to go with a 12-month retainer that covers continuous testing and prioritized scheduling. High level asks: 

- Recommended procurement model (hourly vs retainer) given our roadmap and expected quarterly app changes.
- Required SOW guardrails (evidence transfer, deliverable cadence, data handling, SLAs for critical windows).
- Any non-negotiable legal/insurance items we should force up front.

Attachments: redline_proposal_v1.pdf, pricing_model.xlsx

I think a retainer could be cheaper and give us faster incident response for follow-ups, but I want procurement/legal input before we lock it. Marissa, can you do a quick cost comparison vs last year's spend? Laura, please flag anything you see in the proposal that needs to be redlined. Aditya — curious on feasibility for sandbox access timelines if we go retainer and want quarterly assessments.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Manager, Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 02 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope

Jonas —

Quick notes after skimming the pricing_model.xlsx:

- Retainer (12mo) option: ~25% discount vs list hourly when you amortize planned hours (we'd need to commit to a minimum monthly buy). Offers prioritized scheduling and a dedicated project manager.
- Hourly: flexible, but we pay premium for quick turnarounds and it can be unpredictable during peak cycles.

My recommendation (sales side): push for a retainer with a scalable hours bank + rollover (use it or lose less aggressive). Negotiate a fixed response SLA for critical findings and a requirement for SOC2 evidence before signature. Ask for a lower hourly uplift for out-of-scope work.

I added the HubSpot deal link here: https://hubspot.example/app/deal/1234567 — I can set up a 30-min vendor negotiation call tomorrow morning if that helps.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope

Thanks Jonas — appreciate the context. A few clarifications from our side and a conservative retainer construct we can offer: 

1) Retainer option (recommended for continuous programs): 12-month term, 120 hours/year baseline (10 hrs/month) at $14k/month (prepaid). Unused hours roll over quarterly up to 30 hours. Priority triage within 24 hours for critical P1 findings. Includes dedicated PM and quarterly executive summary.

2) Hourly option: $275/hr for standard testers, $420/hr for senior red team members. No priority scheduling guarantee; peak turnaround timeline 7-14 business days.

3) Deliverables: full report (findings + remediation steps), executive summary, one remediation verification test within 30 days for high severity items. Evidence transfer via SFTP with PGP encrypted bundles or secure portal upload.

Attached: SOW_retainer_draft.docx (scope + SLA wording). Happy to redline per your legal feedback.

Alex Kim
Principal Consultant
Redline Security

Subject: Re: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope

Alex —

Thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of follow-ups before we involve legal: 

- Evidence handling: we prefer uploads to our secure portal (SAML/OAuth) instead of SFTP; can you support short-lived credentials or push to a customer-only bucket? Avoiding PGP key management would help our infra team.
- Remediation verification: can you confirm a SLA for the verification test (e.g., verification within 14 days of patch completion)?
- Data retention & reproduction: we need explicit retention windows for collected artifacts and a commitment to destroy copies on request (with signed attestation).

Marissa — on the cost side, if we commit to 120 hours and only consume 90, what's the refund/credit policy? Also, do you see any procurement risk if we push for a monthly prepaid model?

Laura/Aditya — please see Alex's SOW draft (attached). Laura, if you want to do a live redline session tomorrow, we can host.

Jonas

Date: Sat, 04 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redline Security engagement model evaluation and preferred SOW scope

Team —

Reviewed Alex's draft this morning. High-level redlines and required items before procurement can approve: 

- Insurance: need certificate of liability (min $5M) + cyber liability (min $3M) listed on the SOW.
- SOC2 Type II: require attestation within the last 12 months or an active SOC2 readiness report plus compensating controls.
- Data retention/destruction: add clause for artifact retention windows (30 days by default, extendable by request) and certified destruction upon request with signed attestation.
- SLA enforcement: credits for missed response SLAs; specify measurable metrics (TTR, TTRP for remediation verification).
- IP & reporting: ensure Redwood retains all remediation IP and anonymized data sharing for vendor marketing is opt-in only.

I also attached a marked-up SOW with inline comments: redlines_markups.docx. If Redline can accept these items, procurement is comfortable with a retainer model (prepaid with quarterly reconciliation). Otherwise, we should default to hourly for the first engagement.

Laura Bennett
Director, Legal & Procurement
Redwood Inference
